alerts.title: Rising creatinine on TDF in pregnancy
alerts.message: TDF is associated with renal toxicity including elevated creatinine. Patient's creatinine rose from 0.8 to 1.1 mg/dL within 10 weeks of starting TDF, and eGFR is 78 mL/min/1.73m². Pregnancy normally increases GFR, so a creatinine rise during pregnancy is particularly concerning and strengthens the case for drug attribution. Urinalysis is normal with no proteinuria, which argues against significant tubular damage. DTG can also cause a small creatinine increase via inhibition of tubular secretion, but a 0.3 mg/dL rise in 10 weeks during pregnancy exceeds what would be expected from DTG alone. Dehydration or pre-eclampsia are unlikely given normal BP, no oedema, and negative urine protein.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat creatinine and eGFR promptly. If creatinine continues to rise, consider switching TDF to TAF per guideline alternatives for pregnant women.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring frequency in pregnancy
alerts.message: Guidelines specify viral load monitoring every 3 months for pregnant and lactating women. Patient's current viral load is 89 copies/mL (suppressed), measured approximately 10 weeks after ART initiation. A follow-up viral load at 3 months on ART is due soon and should not be missed, as this is the next scheduled monitoring point per pregnancy-specific timelines. The clinician's plan contains no documented orders for repeat viral load monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule repeat viral load at 3 months on ART (approximately 2 weeks from now) and every 3 months thereafter during pregnancy per pregnancy monitoring guidelines.

alerts.title: No clinician assessment or plan documented
alerts.message: No assessment or plan was documented for this pregnant patient on ART for 10 weeks. Key clinical decisions are missing: renal monitoring plan for rising creatinine on TDF, scheduling of next viral load per pregnancy-specific 3-monthly intervals, and evaluation of the 6 kg weight gain (62 to 68 kg) which may reflect normal pregnancy but warrants assessment for TDF-related or DTG-related weight gain. Documentation of a management plan is essential for safe continuity of care.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a complete assessment and plan addressing renal monitoring, viral load scheduling, weight gain evaluation, and routine antenatal care coordination.
